title: Affine Hecke Algebras Beyond Type A

items.title: The Iwahori–Matsumoto affine Hecke algebra of a based root datum
items.statement: Fix a reduced based root datum, an associated affine Coxeter system with its length-zero symmetries, and positive parameters constant on the extended affine conjugacy classes. The item defines the Iwahori–Matsumoto affine Hecke algebra and its parameter normalization.
items.strategy: Define the root-data and affine-Coxeter inputs, then specify the quadratic, braid, and length-zero symmetry relations without asserting a Bernstein basis.
items.axiom_use: None; the algebra is a quotient of a free algebra on the stated generators.

sources.title: Maarten Solleveld, Affine Hecke Algebras and Their Representations
sources.locator: §§1.2–1.4, PDF pp. 8–12: based root data, affine Coxeter groups, positive parameter systems, and the Iwahori–Matsumoto and Bernstein conventions.

sources.title: Dan Ciubotaru, Tutorial on Affine Hecke Algebras
sources.locator: §1, Definition 1.2, PDF p. 1; §3, PDF pp. 4–5: generic affine Hecke parameters, Iwahori–Matsumoto normalization, and the Bernstein–Lusztig presentation.

items.title: The extended Iwahori–Matsumoto basis
items.statement: For the affine Coxeter subgroup and its length-zero symmetry group in the Iwahori–Matsumoto definition, the elements T_w U_omega form a basis over the parameter ring.
items.strategy: Apply the generic Coxeter standard-basis theorem to the affine Coxeter subgroup and use the direct-sum basis of its semidirect product with the length-zero symmetry group.
items.axiom_use: None; the bases and group action are given explicitly, and only finite-support expansions are used.

sources.title: Maarten Solleveld, Affine Hecke Algebras and Their Representations
sources.locator: §1.2, PDF pp. 8–9, and §1.4, PDF pp. 10–12: affine Coxeter and extended affine groups and their Iwahori–Matsumoto presentation.

items.title: The formal Bernstein presentation for a reduced based root datum
items.statement: For a reduced based root datum and affine parameter data, define the formal algebra generated by the lattice group algebra, the finite Hecke generators, and length-zero symmetries, with the Bernstein cross-relations in both root-lattice cases.
items.strategy: State the root-datum conventions, parameter normalization, two Bernstein cross-relations, and quotient presentation; claim no PBW basis or equivalence to the Iwahori–Matsumoto algebra in the definition.
items.axiom_use: None; a quotient of a free associative algebra is defined without a choice principle.

items.title: The Bernstein cross-relation quotients are Laurent polynomials
items.statement: For each simple root and lattice element, the quotient in the applicable Bernstein cross-relation belongs to the group algebra C[Y], including the special alpha-in-2X denominator.
items.strategy: Write the numerator as a monomial times 1 minus a power of the corresponding coroot monomial and use a finite geometric sum, separately for odd and even pairings.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof is a finite algebraic identity for each lattice element.

sources.title: Maarten Solleveld, Affine Hecke Algebras and Their Representations
sources.locator: §1.3, Definition 1.6, PDF p. 10: divisibility in the Bernstein cross-relations for both parameter cases.

sources.title: Dan Ciubotaru, Tutorial on Affine Hecke Algebras
sources.locator: §3, Theorem 3.1 and the following discussion, PDF p. 4: divisibility of theta_x minus theta_s(x) by the displayed root or doubled-root denominator.

items.title: A positive real p-adic parameter is not a finite quantum-characteristic specialization
items.statement: Over C, every positive parameter q greater than 1 has quantum characteristic infinity and cannot equal a root-of-unity parameter of finite quantum characteristic.
items.strategy: Use positivity of every finite geometric sum for q greater than 1 and modulus one for roots of unity.
items.axiom_use: None; only ordered-field inequalities and the stated definition of quantum characteristic are used.

items.title: The general Bernstein PBW theorem remains a local proof obligation
items.statement: The local inventory records the source-reported Bernstein PBW theorem and its exact missing proof route without treating a citation as a logical supplier.
items.strategy: Separate the proved Iwahori–Matsumoto basis and quotient well-definedness from the unproved general Bernstein cross-relations, PBW basis, and presentation isomorphism.
items.axiom_use: None; this is a nonlogical status remark.

items.title: The tempered and Langlands classification remains a local proof obligation
items.statement: The source-reported affine-Hecke Langlands classification is stated with its positive real parameter, parabolic, temperedness, and positive-position hypotheses; its complete local proof and exact p-adic group interface remain unresolved.
items.strategy: Record the complete source formulation and isolate its required local helpers and consumers without claiming theorem acceptance.
items.axiom_use: None; this is a nonlogical status remark.

title: Affine Hecke Algebras Beyond Type A: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A rank-two affine B2 Hecke algebra with unequal parameters
items.statement: The based B2 root datum with X the weight lattice and Y the coroot lattice gives an affine B2 Coxeter system with long-root parameter 2 and short-root parameter 3; its Iwahori–Matsumoto generators and basis are checked explicitly.
items.strategy: Verify the root datum, affine simple reflections, Coxeter labels, parameter constancy, normalization, and basis using the A-page affine Hecke items.
items.axiom_use: None; all lattices, reflections, parameters, and bases are explicit or are supplied by a proved Coxeter Hecke theorem.

items.title: A positive p-adic parameter and a finite root-of-unity parameter
items.statement: Over C, the split p-adic parameter 3 has quantum characteristic infinity, whereas the finite type-A parameter i has quantum characteristic 4; this compares parameter regimes and asserts no algebra equivalence or inequivalence.
items.strategy: Compute the two geometric sums and compare the parameter moduli, retaining the explicit boundary between the positive-real and root-of-unity settings.
items.axiom_use: None; the checks are finite scalar computations.
